words.exampleSentence: La mariposa monarca vuela miles de kilómetros hasta los bosques de México.
words.exampleTranslation: The monarch butterfly flies thousands of kilometers to the forests of Mexico.
words.funFact: The Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve in Michoacán, Mexico is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

words.exampleSentence: ¡Qué chévere verte después de tanto tiempo!
words.exampleTranslation: How great to see you after so much time!
words.etymology: From Afro-Cuban / Efik origin via the Caribbean
words.funFact: 'Chévere' is one of the most beloved and ubiquitous colloquial words across the Caribbean, Colombia, Venezuela, and beyond.

words.exampleSentence: Un pequeño colibrí se detuvo a beber néctar.
words.exampleTranslation: A small hummingbird paused to drink nectar.
words.funFact: In ancient Aztec mythology, Huitzilopochtli was symbolized by the hummingbird.

words.exampleSentence: Vamos a viajar en carro por toda la costa.
words.exampleTranslation: We are going to travel by car along the entire coast.
words.funFact: While Spain uses 'coche', most Latin American countries use 'carro' or 'auto'.

words.exampleSentence: Salimos de madrugada para evitar el tráfico.
words.exampleTranslation: We left in the early morning to avoid traffic.

words.exampleSentence: Trabajo con mi computadora portátil en la oficina.
words.exampleTranslation: I work with my laptop computer at the office.
words.etymology: Borrowed into American Spanish from English 'computer' / Latin 'computare'
words.funFact: In Spain, people say 'el ordenador', whereas Latin America uniformly uses 'la computadora' (or 'el computador').

words.exampleSentence: Tuvimos una plática muy amena y agradable tomando café.
words.exampleTranslation: We had a very pleasant chat while drinking coffee.
words.etymology: From the verb 'platicar' (to chat/talk), especially prevalent in Mexico and Central America

words.exampleTranslation: Could you give me your cell phone number?
words.funFact: Spain uses 'el móvil', while Latin America says 'el celular'.

words.exampleSentence: Mantenemos viva la esperanza de construir un futuro mejor.
words.exampleTranslation: We keep alive the hope of building a better future.

words.exampleSentence: El girasol es originario de las Américas y fue domesticado hace miles de años.
words.exampleTranslation: The sunflower is native to the Americas and was domesticated thousands of years ago.
words.funFact: Indigenous peoples of the Americas cultivated sunflowers for food and medicinal dye long before European contact.
